summary.intent: Get a comprehensive analysis of what the code reviews and slop reviews revealed across Callisto (plus Caliper and monokl reports): recurring mistake patterns, whether more instances exist, whether the wisp-plugins structure is at fault, and what is generic vs repo-specific. The user then pushed for a more thorough investigation, and questioned why runners were set to macos-15 instead of macos-latest.
summary.outcome: Ran two read-only sweeps (Rust and shell/workflow/CI), verified key claims, reproduced E170 on the real binary, and saved a full analysis to .claude/plans/. After the user objected, the macOS runner lines were changed from macos-15 back to macos-latest, pushed, and PR #445 retitled; no other fixes were made.

repo: The generated matrix workflow template never detaches HEAD, so `release plan`, `execute` and `build-python` hit E170 (requires a detached HEAD) in downstream repos; Callisto's own release workflow checks out `ref: <sha>`, which hides it.

`callisto release` (local/simple route) uses ReleaseCheckout::AnyHead, while plan/execute/build-python require Detached, so monokl's E170 on the simple template may be an older binary or a different precondition (unconfirmed).

`just ci` is a strict subset of GitHub CI (CI adds machete, features-boundary, check-api, per-crate coverage, --locked, MSRV, artifact preflight and contract scripts), explaining local green / CI red.

Template pins drift from repo pins (upload-artifact v7.0.1 vs v7.0.2, download-artifact v8.0.1 vs v8.0.2) because dependabot edits only .github and verify-action-pins.sh scans only *.yml/*.yaml, never .tmpl.
`gh attestation verify` (gh 2.103.3) has --source-ref and --cert-identity but no --signer-ref; test stubs accept any flag so a wrong flag would stay green.
pypi observation uses an unauthenticated curl while publish uses TWINE_* credentials, so a private index returns 401 and settles indeterminate.
RELEASE_CREDENTIALS exists as diverging copies in the cli runner, graph registry provider and test harness.
The fake git/cargo in release_harness.rs encode old contracts: record_pushed_tag resolves refs/tags/$3, and fake `cargo publish` ignores --registry.
Entire trail list is capped at 50 and omits changes; trails must be iterated by number.
The sandbox cannot write ~/.cargo, so a build needing a new dependency required running unsandboxed.
.claude/plans is git-excluded in both the main checkout and worktrees.

code.finding: Only place the DetachedHead E170 precondition is raised, when checkout==Detached but HEAD is attached.
actions/checkout in plan job has no ref:, leaving HEAD attached on push; same at build-python (~188) and execute (~222).
`adapter.classify(&output).map(|_outcome| ())` discards AlreadyPublished, so the receipt records Published instead of AlreadySatisfied.
ls-remote failure returns an empty Vec, indistinguishable from 'no tags missing'.
Summary prints 'Released N package(s)' from decision entries even when all operations were AlreadySatisfied.
detect_rate_limit and detect_auth_failure use loose substring matches (429, 401, 'rate', 'auth') that can misclassify errors.
Uses a different taiki-e/install-action SHA (1168f681…) than the other 19 uses (86f7a0ff…).
Download failure falls through to unattested `cargo install` fallback, bypassing verification=require; no retry or timeout.
